Answer.description: An answer to a question event: one of its options.
Answer.title: Answer

BoardRef.description: A board revision, as named in its `demos/<board>/*.json` file.
BoardRef.title: BoardRef

board.description: The board revision the build was checked against; null for a design without a board

maps.description: Analysis maps available for the build
maps.title: Maps

source_url.description: The CAD code that produced the build (`BuildSource`)
source_url.title: Source Url

board_url.description: The board revision named by `board`, in the board JSON format (`backend/app/boards/SCHEMA.md`); 404 when `board` is null
board_url.title: Board Url

step_url.description: STEP of the build, null until exported
step_url.title: Step Url

restored_from.description: The earlier build whose design this build restores (undo in the history)
restored_from.title: Restored From

failure.description: Why a failed build couldn't be built, in plain words for the user (never internal error text); null for a ready build
failure.title: Failure

origin.description: The file the build came from, for a build no message made (an import, or the existing design an example opens on); null otherwise

BuildOrigin.description: Where a build that no message made came from, so the chat can say so where it happened.

kind.description: `import`: a file the user imported; `existing`: the existing design an example opens on, read from its file
kind.title: Kind

BuildOrigin.title: BuildOrigin

mode.description: manual: only accepted changes are applied; auto: all start accepted
mode.title: Mode

base_build.description: Build of the design the run started from
base_build.title: Base Build

build.description: Build of the accepted changes, once checked
build.title: Build

message_id.description: The run's message; null for a review outside a run
message_id.title: Message Id

CheckLink.description:
A check that proves (or argues against) a change.

`before` is the check on the design the run started from, `alone` on that design plus this
change only, and `after` on the current build (the accepted changes); null when that build
has no such check or doesn't exist yet.

title.description: The result's title on the checks strip, as people read it
title.title: Title

effect.description: `fixes`: fails before, passes with the change alone; `breaks`: the reverse; `related`: about the same component or feature
effect.title: Effect

CheckLink.title: CheckLink

not_applicable.description: Standards that do not apply to this design
not_applicable.title: Not Applicable

build_id.description: The build it was pinned on
build_id.title: Build Id

face_id.description: Stable face ID: the comment survives rebuilds
face_id.title: Face Id

point.description: Where it was pinned, on the build it was pinned on
point.title: Point

feature.description: The feature that made the face: if a rebuild drops the face ID, the pin moves to the nearest face of the same feature
feature.title: Feature

anchor.description: Centre of the face on the build it was pinned on. On a later build the pin keeps its offset from the face's centre, so it follows the face when it moves
anchor.title: Anchor

location.description: Where the pin is on the build the list was asked for (the latest by default); null when the build no longer has the face or its feature

request.description: Set once the comment is sent to Claude; null for a note

CommentEvent.description:
A comment was pinned, replied to, sent, answered or resolved: the whole comment as it
is now, located on the latest build.

message_id.description: The run, for Claude's replies while it runs
message_id.title: Message Id

CommentEvent.title: CommentEvent

message_id.description: The run that wrote it, for Claude's replies
message_id.title: Message Id

CommentRequest.description: The comment was sent to Claude: the run that handles it.
CommentRequest.title: CommentRequest

ConflictConstraint.description: One side of a conflict: a locked parameter, a team standard or a board part.

id.description: Parameter path, standard ID or component reference
id.title: Id

label.description: What to call it, e.g. the standard's title
label.title: Label

relation.description: How `value` binds: a lock or a part's height is `=`, a `min` standard `>=`, a `max` standard `<=`
relation.title: Relation

value.description: The locked value, the standard's value, or the height
value.title: Value

best.description: Best achievable value when only this constraint gives way; null when no value of it resolves the conflict (a board part can't change)
best.title: Best

locations.description: Where on the model it acts
locations.title: Locations

ConflictConstraint.title: ConflictConstraint

Constraint.description:
One constraint of the design's spec, shown as a chip above the chat input.

Every constraint is a team standard (`standards.yaml`) with the value the design must
meet, so its check enforces it. The value is the standard's own (`source: standard`), one
the user gave in a message (`user`, with their words in `quote`) or a chip edit (`edit`).

label.description: The chip text, e.g. "Minimum wall thickness ≥ 2.5 mm"
label.title: Label

source.description: `standard`: from standards.yaml; `user`: from the user's words; `edit`: the chip was edited
source.title: Source

quote.description: The user's words it came from
quote.title: Quote

message_id.description: The message the user's words are in
message_id.title: Message Id

Constraint.title: Constraint

ConstraintConflict.description: Locked values, standards and the board that can't all be met (conflict detection).

over_by.description: How far apart the constraints are, in mm
over_by.title: Over By

ConstraintConflict.title: ConstraintConflict

ConstraintsEvent.description: The design's spec changed: every constraint, as the chips show them.
ConstraintsEvent.title: ConstraintsEvent

ErrorEvent.description:
The run stopped. `message` says plainly what happened, whether anything was lost and
what to do; `retryable` offers Retry (`POST .../retry`), which picks up from the design
and builds so far.

reason.description: Why, as a code; null: unknown
reason.title: Reason

ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

FieldDelta.description:
One value that differs: its dot path inside the changed element, before and after
(null when absent).
FieldDelta.title: FieldDelta

face.description: A face ID of the build's mesh
face.title: Face

feature.description: The feature that created the face
feature.title: Feature

value.description: The measured value the query compared, if it compared one
value.title: Value

status.description: `found` with matches, `none` when the query was understood and nothing matches, `unclear` when part of it wasn't understood (see `question`)
status.title: Status

understood.description: What the query was read as, in words
understood.title: Understood

question.description: Set when `unclear`: what to ask the user, with suggestions
question.title: Question

FoundEvent.description:
Claude looked for parts of the model from chat (`find_in_model`): the canvas
highlights the matched faces, and the chat lists them, ready to send back as the
selection. An unclear query has no matches: the chat shows what was understood and the
question.

build_id.description: The build whose mesh faces the matches name
build_id.title: Build Id

FoundEvent.title: FoundEvent

path.description: Parameter path of the changed element (`openings.<id>`)
path.title: Path

feature.description: Feature tag on the mesh, e.g. `opening_Q4`, if it has one
feature.title: Feature

move.description: How far it moved in x and y, mm (modified elements only)
move.title: Move

Location.description:
Where on the model something is: a point (mm, board coordinates) and the faces and edges
it concerns, by their stable mesh IDs.
Location.title: Location

text.description: May be empty when `answer` is given
text.title: Text

model.description: Model ID from `contracts/models.json`; the server picks if null
model.title: Model

mode.description: Auto applies changes; Manual proposes them
mode.title: Mode

standards.description: A standards set ID (`GET /api/standards`) for the agent and checks to use. Given with the session's first message; a later message may repeat it but not change it
standards.title: Standards

comments.description: Comments sent to Claude ("Send to Claude"): one run handles them all and answers each in its own thread. `text` may be empty
comments.title: Comments

MessageQueue.description: The messages waiting for the current run to end, in the order they will be sent.

paused.description: Claude's question is open: the next message waits until it is answered (it is never taken as the answer), or until it is sent anyway (`POST .../queue/{item}/send`)
paused.title: Paused

MessageQueue.title: MessageQueue

categories.description: safety: what kind of product it is, e.g. "a product for children"
categories.title: Categories

regulations.description: safety: kinds of regulations that may apply; none were checked
regulations.title: Regulations

region.description: safety: the region the user named; null when unknown
region.title: Region

NoticeEvent.title: NoticeEvent

PlanEvent.description: Claude's build plan for a new design, shown before any edit.
PlanEvent.title: PlanEvent

text.description: A progress line, e.g. "Fixing the cutout · round 1 of 4"
text.title: Text

id.description: Stable within the set: the parameter path
id.title: Id

rounds.description: Fix rounds whose edits touched it
rounds.title: Rounds

comment.description: The comment this change answers (a comment sent to Claude): its thread shows the change with accept, reject and Undo
comment.title: Comment

location.description: The spot on the model the question is about, to pin it at

conflict.description: Set when Claude asks because the constraints can't all be met

QueueEvent.description:
The session's message queue changed (a message queued, edited, moved, removed or sent,
or a question pausing it): the whole queue as it is now, so every tab shows the same.

sent.description: The queued message this change sent, if it sent one
sent.title: Sent

QueueEvent.title: QueueEvent

QueuedMessage.description:
A message sent while Claude was working: it waits in the session's queue and is sent,
as a normal message, once the runs before it have ended (`GET .../queue`).

message.description: What is sent when its turn comes (text, attachments, selection, standards, model, effort and mode); never an answer

QueuedMessage.title: QueuedMessage

RiskFix.description:
The proposed change that answers a risk: what it sets, and the checks of the design with
it alone. A fix can't break a check that passes without it.

edits.description: Parameter path to new value; `code` for new code
edits.title: Edits

resolves.description: The risk is gone on the build with the fix alone
resolves.title: Resolves

RiskFix.title: RiskFix

RiskFlag.description: A risk the checks don't block, named in one line in chat, with a fix.

id.description: `<kind>:<feature or check>`, unique in the set
id.title: Id

kind.description: `thick`: a section that sinks when molded; `thin`, `low_draft`: an analysis spot no failing check covers; `near_limit`: a passing check close to its limit
kind.title: Kind

message.description: The one line said in chat
message.title: Message

RiskFlag.title: RiskFlag

build.description: The build the risks were found on
build.title: Build

RiskLocation.description:
Where a risk is: the part, the feature or component, the faces when the analysis names
them, and a point (mm, board coordinates) when known.
RiskLocation.title: RiskLocation

message_id.description: The run's message; null for a review outside a run
message_id.title: Message Id

Selection.description: What the user selected on the model when they sent the message.

part.description: The part everything selected is on; null across parts
part.title: Part

components.description: Board components selected (reference designators). Their opening faces are not added to `faces`
components.title: Components

Selection.title: Selection

delta.description: Text tokens to append to the message
delta.title: Delta

TitleEvent.description:
The session was renamed: by Claude, naming the part it designs (`message_id` of its run),
or by the user (`message_id` null). The header and Recents show the new name.
TitleEvent.title: TitleEvent

UserMessageEvent.description:
The user sent a message (typed, an answer, a queued message sent, a revision load, a
Retry): the message as stored, so every tab shows it, not only the one that sent it.
UserMessageEvent.title: UserMessageEvent

title: Session server-sent event (the JSON in each event's data line)
